versions.notes: SevenCode 1.0.27 — one Node bundle (3 475 382 bytes, sha256 91311f19a31f80196e36e32bcd217e745048ecf33d08f0bca61b3e70aedec5d1), which is why kind is `file` and one artefact serves every platform: the publisher serves the CLI as the single executable it is, and covey writes it rather than unpacking something of ours (#288). The digest is the one the publisher itself announces at /api/v1/cli/version, so it is theirs and not a measurement of ours. The address is `latest`, so a release upstream moves the bytes under a name that stays — that is why the version and the digest stand beside it and why a new release is a new entry rather than an edit. Fetching it needs a login: the agent's own `sevencode_api_token` opens it, carried to the one install that needs it and stored nowhere (#289); COVEY_SEVENCODE_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN stays as the way for a host that holds a token of its own, a mirror with nothing in covey behind it. Either way header and value come together as the endpoint wants them (Bearer sc_…), and the digest is what decides whether the bytes may run. Whoever has no token points COVEY_ENGINE_CATALOG_URL at a catalogue of their own — the engine is then an image question, as it was before this document.
